header.value: X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 (written X-Shopify-Hmac-SHA256 on the verify page; header names are case-insensitive, HTTP/2 often lowercases them). HTTPS deliveries only.
header.quote: Base64-encoded HMAC signature for verifying the delivery came from Shopify. HTTPS only.

header_case.quote: Treat header names as case-insensitive in your code, as HTTP/2 often lowercases them.

scheme.value: HMAC-SHA256, base64 encoded, keyed with the app client secret.
scheme.quote: compute HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your app's client secret as the key, then compare it to the decoded header value.

signed_content.value: The raw request body only (no timestamp or id is part of the signed content).
signed_content.quote: generated using your app's client secret and the raw request body.

header_format.value: A single base64 string, no prefix or key=value pairs. The docs example decodes both the computed digest and the header from base64 before comparing with crypto.timingSafeEqual.

secret_source.value: The app's client secret (the app credentials), not a per-subscription secret.
secret_source.quote: generated using your app's client secret and the raw request body.
secret_source.short: The app's client secret (one per app)

secret_scope.value: Per app: one client secret signs every webhook the app receives, across all shops and topics.
secret_scope.quote: compute HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body using your app's client secret as the key

timestamp_tolerance.value: not stated by the provider (the signature covers only the body; X-Shopify-Triggered-At exists but no replay window is described)

rotation.value: After rotating the app client secret, up to an hour may pass before digests use the new secret. Dual-signature behaviour is not described.
rotation.quote: If you rotate your app's client secret, it can take up to an hour for the HMAC digest to be generated using the new secret.

raw_body_note.value: Capture the raw body before any body parser; place verification middleware before body parsing; ensure encoding is correct.
raw_body_note.quote: HMAC verification requires the raw request body. If you're using a body parser middleware like express.json(), it parses the body before your verification code runs.

verify_always.value: Verify before trusting the payload; skip only in development with mock tools. Not required for Google Pub/Sub or Amazon EventBridge deliveries.
verify_always.quote: Always verify HMAC before trusting payload contents.

node.value: shopify.webhooks.validate({ rawBody: req.body, rawRequest: req, rawResponse: res }) returns { valid, topic, domain } (shopify-api library); React Router template: authenticate.webhook(request) from ../shopify.server verifies before the handler runs

python.value: not stated by the provider on the pages read

dotnet.value: not stated by the provider on the pages read

published_test_vector_note.value: The docs print only code, plus an example header value in the reference (X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256: xT6yH5jZ...) with no secret or body; there is no complete worked example.

method_and_content_type.value: HTTP POST with a JSON payload; the reference example request shows Content-Type: application/json. Deliveries can also go to Google Pub/Sub or Amazon EventBridge instead of HTTPS.
method_and_content_type.quote: For HTTPS destinations, Shopify sends an HTTP POST with a JSON payload in the request body and delivery metadata in HTTP headers.

content_type_example.value: Example request headers include Content-Type: application/json.

event_type_location.value: X-Shopify-Topic header (for example products/update). The body does not name the topic.

delivery_id.value: X-Shopify-Webhook-Id identifies one delivery (dedupe on it). X-Shopify-Event-Id is shared by all deliveries produced by the same merchant action, so two subscriptions to one topic give different Webhook-Ids and the same Event-Id.
delivery_id.quote: A unique composite key per delivery. Use to identify and deduplicate individual deliveries.
delivery_id.short: X-Shopify-Webhook-Id (X-Shopify-Event-Id is shared per merchant action)

event_id.value: X-Shopify-Event-Id: shared across deliveries from one merchant action.
event_id.quote: A unique ID shared across all deliveries produced by the same merchant action.

event_id_note.value: Different Webhook-Id, same Event-Id for multiple subscriptions on one topic.
event_id_note.quote: Each has a different X-Shopify-Webhook-Id but shares the same X-Shopify-Event-Id.

other_headers.value: X-Shopify-Shop-Domain (myshopify.com domain of the store), X-Shopify-API-Version (API version used to serialize the payload), X-Shopify-Triggered-At (timestamp of when Shopify triggered the delivery), X-Shopify-Name (optional, your subscription name).
other_headers.quote: The API version used to serialize the payload.

handshake.value: not stated by the provider (no challenge or ping on subscription)

batching.value: One delivery per qualifying change, with one JSON resource payload (no arrays described). include_fields can shrink the payload; identical small payloads in a short window are debounced (later one dropped).
batching.quote: Each qualifying change sends a webhook delivery to the destination configured in your subscription's uri.

debouncing.value: With include_fields, identical payloads close together can be dropped; include a field that always changes, such as updated_at.
debouncing.quote: Shopify debounces deliveries with identical payloads that arrive within a short time window, dropping the later one.

api_version_header.value: X-Shopify-API-Version on HTTPS deliveries; for Pub/Sub and EventBridge the version is in the message payload. Version for app-specific (TOML) subscriptions comes from webhooks.api_version; for shop-specific subscriptions from the request URL used to create them.
api_version_header.quote: Each delivery includes the API version that serialized its payload.

success_status.value: A 200-range status. Anything outside 200-299, including 3xx redirects, is an error.
success_status.quote: Any response outside the 200 range, including 3XX codes, is treated as an error.

response_deadline.value: 1 second connection timeout and 5 seconds for the whole request.
response_deadline.quote: Shopify has a one-second connection timeout and a five-second timeout for the entire request.
response_deadline.short: 1 second to connect, 5 seconds in all

keep_alive.value: Shopify reuses connections; keep HTTP Keep-Alive enabled on the endpoint.
keep_alive.quote: Ensure Keep-Alive is enabled on your endpoint to reduce overhead from concurrent requests.

retries.value: 8 retries over the next 4 hours after no response or an error. The retry interval grows after each failure. After 8 failed attempts Shopify stops delivering that webhook.
retries.quote: If Shopify receives no response or an error, it retries 8 times over the next 4 hours.
retries.short: 8 retries over 4 hours, then Admin API subscriptions are deleted

retries_interval.value: Interval before the next retry increases each time.
retries_interval.quote: Each time a delivery fails, the interval before the next retry increases.

retries_stop.value: No delivery attempts after the 8th failure.
retries_stop.quote: After 8 failed delivery attempts, Shopify stops attempting delivery.

disabling.value: After 8 consecutive failures the subscription is automatically deleted if it was configured through the Admin API (shop-specific). Warning emails go to the app's emergency developer email. App-specific subscriptions defined in shopify.app.toml are not deleted by Shopify on failure. Removed subscriptions get no deliveries until recreated.
disabling.quote: After 8 consecutive failures, the subscription is automatically deleted if it was configured using the Admin API.

disabling_app_specific.value: TOML-defined subscriptions survive failures; Admin API subscriptions are deleted.
disabling_app_specific.quote: Failing subscriptions will not be deleted by Shopify.

disabling_emails.value: Warning emails to the emergency developer address.
disabling_emails.quote: Warning emails are sent to the app's emergency developer email address.

disabling_recreate.value: Fix the cause and recreate removed subscriptions.
disabling_recreate.quote: Fix the issue, then recreate the webhook subscriptions.

ordering.value: Not guaranteed within a topic or across topics for the same resource (for example products/update can arrive before products/create). Use X-Shopify-Triggered-At or the payload updated_at to order.
ordering.quote: Shopify doesn't guarantee ordering within a topic, or across different topics for the same resource.

ordering_timestamps.value: Order with header or payload timestamps.
ordering_timestamps.quote: Shopify recommends using timestamps provided in the header (X-Shopify-Triggered-At) or in the payload itself (updated_at) to organize webhooks.

duplicates.value: Possible (for example after a network timeout or a retry). Make processing idempotent or store X-Shopify-Webhook-Id and skip seen ids, returning success.
duplicates.quote: Shopify minimizes duplicate deliveries, but your app might receive the same webhook more than once

delivery_not_guaranteed.value: Delivery is not guaranteed; run reconciliation jobs (many GraphQL queries accept updated_at filters).
delivery_not_guaranteed.quote: Webhook delivery isn't always guaranteed, and your app can miss or mishandle events for other reasons

delays.value: Webhooks can arrive late (up to a day is mentioned); compare the webhook timestamp to the current time if that matters.
delays.quote: If receiving webhooks up to a day late might cause issues in your app, then compare the timestamp of the webhook to the current date and time.

common.meaning: A new order was created in the shop.

common.quote: products/update fires when an existing product changes; products/create fires when a new one is created.
products/update fires when an existing product changes

common.meaning: The app was uninstalled from a shop.
Mandatory compliance topic: a customer asked the merchant for their stored data.
common.quote: Requests to view stored customer data

common.meaning: Mandatory compliance topic: delete a customer's data.
Mandatory compliance topic: delete a shop's data after uninstall.

mandatory_topics.quote: Every app that's distributed through the Shopify App Store must subscribe to the following compliance webhook topics:

scope.value: Mandatory for apps distributed through the Shopify App Store (public apps); the docs example config comment elsewhere says public apps only. Apps are rejected in review without them.
scope.quote: If you don't provide URLs for the mandatory compliance webhooks, or your app doesn't respond to these webhooks as required, then your app will be rejected

invalid_hmac.value: Respond 401 Unauthorized to an invalid HMAC on a compliance webhook.
invalid_hmac.quote: If a mandatory compliance webhook sends a request with an invalid Shopify HMAC header, then the app must return a 401 Unauthorized HTTP status.

content_type.value: Compliance webhooks are POST with a JSON body and Content-Type application/json.
content_type.quote: The app must handle POST requests with a JSON body and Content-Type header set to application/json sent to mandatory compliance webhooks.

response_and_deadline.value: Answer with a 2xx to confirm receipt, then complete the action within 30 days (unless law requires you to retain the data, in which case do not complete a redaction).
response_and_deadline.quote: Complete the action within 30 days of receiving the request.

shop_redact_timing.value: shop/redact is sent 48 hours after uninstall.
shop_redact_timing.quote: 48 hours after a store owner uninstalls your app, Shopify sends a payload on the shop/redact topic.

customers_redact_timing.value: customers/redact is delayed: 10 days after the request if the customer has no order in six months, otherwise withheld until six months have passed.
customers_redact_timing.quote: If a customer hasn't placed an order in the past six months, then Shopify sends the payload 10 days after the deletion request.

config.value: Subscribe in shopify.app.toml with compliance_topics (not topics); these cannot be subscribed through the Admin API.
config.quote: Cannot be subscribed to using the Admin API.

where_url_is_entered.value: App-specific (recommended): [[webhooks.subscriptions]] in shopify.app.toml with topics and uri, plus [webhooks] api_version; released with 'shopify app deploy' or via Dev Dashboard Versions. Shop-specific: GraphQL Admin API webhookSubscriptionCreate. uri may be an HTTPS URL, a pubsub://project:topic URI or an EventBridge ARN.
where_url_is_entered.quote: uri | Delivery destination. HTTPS URL, AWS EventBridge ARN, or Google Pub/Sub URI.

recommended_destination.value: Shopify recommends Google Pub/Sub; HTTPS needs extra care.
recommended_destination.quote: Shopify recommends using Google Pub/Sub as a cloud-based solution for delivering webhooks.

test_tools.value: 'shopify app webhook trigger --api-version=<version> --address=<destination> --topic=<topic-name>' sends a synthetic webhook to your endpoint; it does not test subscription configuration. Dev Dashboard shows delivery logs (7 days) and metrics.

trigger_limit.value: The trigger does not exercise your real subscription.
trigger_limit.quote: It doesn't test your subscription configuration.

logs_window.value: Delivery logs cover the past 7 days.
logs_window.quote: The Logs page shows individual deliveries filterable by topic, status, and destination shop over the past 7 days.

ip_allowlist.value: not stated by the provider on the pages read

versioning.value: Webhooks are versioned like other Shopify APIs; Shopify recommends updating to the latest stable version each quarter; existing subscriptions keep their earlier version until you update and deploy.
versioning.quote: Shopify recommends updating to the latest stable API version each quarter.

gotchas.value: Answer within 5 seconds; queue work; redirects count as errors.
gotchas.quote: Queuing is a useful pattern for handling bursts of traffic and for ensuring you respond within five seconds.

gotchas.value: Do not rely on webhooks alone; build reconciliation.
gotchas.quote: Your app shouldn't rely on receiving data from Shopify webhooks.

gotchas.value: Failing Admin-API subscriptions are deleted after 8 consecutive failures, silently except for warning emails.
gotchas.quote: After 8 consecutive failures, the subscription is automatically deleted if it was configured using the Admin API.

gotchas.value: Body parser middleware before verification breaks HMAC.
gotchas.quote: Place your webhook verification middleware before any body parsing middleware in your app.

gotchas.value: A shop-specific to app-specific migration can double-deliver unless old subscriptions are removed first.
gotchas.quote: remove any existing webhook subscriptions to the same topics. This avoids potential conflicts and duplicate notifications.

gotchas.value: Compliance webhooks cannot be created through the Admin API, only in app config or Dev Dashboard.
gotchas.quote: You can create mandatory compliance webhook subscriptions in Dev Dashboard or by updating your app configuration file.

conflicts.topic: What happens to a subscription after repeated failures
conflicts.note: Pages differ in scope, not in numbers. The verify page and the subscriptions table say deletion applies to Admin API (shop-specific) subscriptions and not to TOML app-specific ones; the troubleshoot page states removal without that qualification.

sources.quote: Failing subscriptions will not be deleted by Shopify.
but if failures persist, the subscription is removed.
